To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) profile likelihood is the most reliable statistical method for dark matter detection; (2) for a given target, the statistical uncertainty on the WIMP mass is larger than the uncertainty on the Wimp-nucleon cross section, and the uncertainty on the cross section is larger than the statistical uncertainty on any other parameter; and (3) combining data sets from different targets leads to an improvement of the confidence interval coverage, as well as to a reduction of the statistical bias and uncertainty.

(i) the coverage of confidence regions from a profile-likelyhood analysis is exact or overexact, and hence conservative, for all models we consider; (ii) the probability that unavoidable fluctuations in the data lead to a biased estimate of the dark matter properties is non-negligible for all models we study, and can be substantial for some of them; (iii) the combination of two different targets leads in most cases to an improvement of the coverage properties, as to the statistical bias

the coverage and the bias of future dark matter detection experiments will depend on the model parameters, and that combining data from different targets will improve the reliability of the reconstruction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
fundamental statistical limitations of future experiments, which are often overlooked.
fundamental statistical limitations of dark matter searches and their impact on future experiments.
the fundamental statistical limitations of future direct detection experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the statistical coverage of the profile-likelihood confidence interval is excellent for all the models studied, but that the statistical bias and uncertainty can be large for some of the models.

, for all benchmark models considered, the ton-scale dark matter detection experiments will be able to exclude the standard WIMP scenario, and that a large fraction of them will be able to detect a WIMP signal, but only a small fraction of them will provide a conclusive and reliable measurement of the WIMP properties.
, for a large fraction of the parameter space, the statistical limitations of future direct detection experiments are not as small as one might naively expect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of large statistical fluctuations, the coverage of confidence regions and the bias of reconstructed parameters are not guaranteed to be under control, even for a ton-scale detector.
the statistical uncertainties on the dark matter parameter reconstruction will be much larger than previously anticipated, and that the statistical bias can be substantial.

, for the benchmark models we consider, the statistical coverage properties of ton-scale direct detection experiments are excellent and irreducible uncertainties on the reconstructed parameters are small, even for models leading to a few hundred counts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the context of dark matter direct detection, the coverage properties of approximate confidence intervals are not necessarily guaranteed, and the probability that statistical fluctuations might lead to large uncertainties or bias on reconstructed dark matter parameters can be significant.
, even with a large event rate, the coverage and the bias of future dark matter searches can be large.
the statistical limitations of future direct detection experiments can be quantified and understood.
